title: Rapid Subtractive Patterning of Live Cell Layers with a Microfluidic Probe
protocol: Use capillaries with a 1/16'' (1.59 mm) outer diameter and 0.02'' (0.51 mm) inner diameter for all tubings connected to the syringes.
Obtain appropriate connectors and fittings to interface the MFP head with the syringes.
Use ultrapure water wherever dilutions are necessary.
Clean syringes (250 - 500 µl volume) and syringe plungers by sonication in a 0.5% bleach solution in ultrapure water before and after live cell experiments.
Rinse syringes thoroughly with water.
Fill syringes with water by immersing their tips completely in a water bath and aspirating using the plunger.
Purge liquid while within the water bath with the syringe shaft contacting the seal at the exit of the syringe.
Repeat aspirate and purge until no air bubbles are seen in the syringe columns.
Connect filled syringes to the syringe pumps using Luer-lock connectors.
Use a switch valve mounted on the pumps to direct liquid from the syringe to one of two capillaries leading either to the MFP head or to the liquid reservoirs.
Purge both capillaries with water from the syringes at a flow rate of about 10 - 50 µl/min until about 10 µl of water is left in the syringes.
Pre-insert purged capillaries into an appropriate microfluidic connector/adaptor which interfaces with the channel vias in the head (e.g., M1 connector).
Clean the MFP head by sonication using glassware detergent for standard cleaning or 0.5% bleach for stringent cleaning, for 5 min.
Purge channels with water by immersing the apex in water and applying vacuum to the vias.
Inspect channels under a stereomicroscope for potential obstructions.
Repeat the previous step if necessary due to obstructions.
Mount the clean head on the head holder.
Screw the connector with pre-inserted and purged tubing onto the head.
Screw the head holder to the Z-stage.
Perform endpoint calibration of the X-, Y-, and Z-stages using appropriate software interface according to manufacturer's protocol.
Obtain a crude zero gap distance by bringing the MFP head over a chamber slide without cells and slowly descending in 5 µm steps.
Upon probe contact with the substrate, observe Newton's rings for initial alignment.
Adjust the tilt of the head using a goniometer at the interface of the head and Z-stage to ensure coplanarity of the probe apex to the substrate.
Move the MFP head 20 µm away from the substrate after adjusting the tilt.
Repeat descending, zeroing, and tilt adjustment until Newton's rings are symmetric on contact.
Set the z position which produces symmetric Newton's rings as zero.
Prepare 50 mM NaOH solution as the processing liquid for the inner injection channel.
Prepare extraction buffer solution composed of 1 mM EDTA, 0.5% Tween 20, and 10 µM rhodamine B in 50 mM Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane at pH 8.
Filter all solutions using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Degas all filtered solutions until the dissolved air stops bubbling to the surface.
Purge remnant water from the syringe pumps using the drain line.
Aspirate degassed solutions into the injection syringes at 40 µl/min until full (250 or 500 µl).
Ensure bubble-free filling of the syringes, connectors, and capillaries.
Use a syringe–switch valve–two-capillary system to fill syringes mid-experiment if available.
In absence of switch valve, disconnect capillaries from the head and fill before reconnecting.
Aspirate processing and shielding liquids through the capillaries for use with small volumes during operation.
If large volume preparation possible, fill aspiration syringes containing water directly.
Purge capillaries to MFP head with liquids allocated as defined in 1.4.1 and 1.4.2.
Use extraction buffer solution to shield NaOH in the inner confinement.
Rhodamine component in buffer facilitates visualization of hHFC during operation.
Supplement the extraction buffer with 10% Proteinase K if cells are over-confluent and cell aggregates appear on the cultured surface.
Use a cell culture hood for culturing the cells.
Handle equipment as per regulations set by the biosafety officer of the laboratory.
Adapt protocol and equipment accordingly based on special requirements of specific cell lines.
Perform expansion using standard cell culture protocols in T flasks.
Culture cells in an incubator at 5% CO2 and 37 ºC.
Seed 2×10^5 cells/cm^2 in each of the 2-chamber slides for patterning and culture over 48 hr.
Incubate cells for 45 min with 500 μl cell-tracker dye solution at 10 µM concentration prepared in serum-free medium.
Wash labelled cells with PBS by gently flushing each chamber using a pipette.
Culture cells in serum-supplemented media for patterning experiments.
Obtain a reference image of the cell-tracker-stained cell surface to ensure confluency of the cell layer.
In case cell viability is to be assessed during patterning, stain cells with a Live/Dead cytotoxicity kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Move MFP over the cell monolayer to a gap distance of 50 µm from the glass slide.
Inject NaOH at 6 or 8 μl/min through i2.
Evaluate other flow rates (i.e., QI1, QA1 and QA2) using the flow rules.
Modulate the size of the inner HFC by changing the ratio of QI2/QI1 using injection syringes.
Set QI1 between 1.3 μl/min and 4 μl/min, with QI2 fixed at 8 μl/min.
Inject complete medium from outer-most apertures on MFP head at a flow rate of 20 μl/min to account for evaporation and aspiration during hHFC operation.
Set the stage software to scan the probe head over the cell monolayer in user-defined patterns (by setting X, Y and Z coordinates).
Scan the probe head over the cell monolayer at a scan velocity of 10 µm/s at a gap distance of 50 µm.
With the nested hHFC in operation and in contact with the monolayer, scan the MFP with a trajectory of the desired pattern to effect patterned cell removal.
For a co-culture after the first cell type removal, seed a different cell line to fill the gaps using methods described in section 1.5.
Move between nested and pinched modes by increasing gap distance to control cell removal.
Prepare the sampling station for downstream analysis of the lysate.
Use a 3D printed 8-strip PCR tube holder or an appropriate tube holder capable of being mounted within the scanning range of the head outside the substrate.
Wipe the tube holder with 70% ethanol or other surface decontaminants based on the stringency desired for the application.
Attach the tube holder onto the substrate holder using a magnetic clip.
Position the MFP head 100 µm from the monolayer.
Operate the hHFC with 50 mM NaOH solution as the processing liquid for the inner injection channel.
Set flow rates of 1, 6, -7 and -17.5 µl/min for QI1, QI2, QA1 and QA2 respectively.
Stabilize flow confinement for approximately 10 seconds.
Descend probe head to a gap distance of 50 µm.
Perform NaOH-based local lysis on the chosen sub-population of cells with hHFC.
Collect lysate after lysis is complete (approximately 30 seconds per footprint).
Direct probe head towards tubes in the sampling station.
Eject collected lysate into PCR tubes directly.
Neutralize pH of the lysate by mixing with Tris buffer (1:1 ratio).
Heat lysate to 95 ºC for 30 minutes.
Load lysate into a standard qPCR workflow as set by supplier.
